Source: main at f5d94ca7f9a1a1814a50b4d03908a3a742d2b43c, plus the existing, uncommitted compact comments/reader toolbar changes and the small verification fixes described below. This is local verification, not a production release approval. No deployment, signed app installation, or Git commit was made.

Results

Check Result
API recommendation/OpenAlex/configuration contracts 27 passed; the separately executed live test is excluded
Reading-feed and ranking crates, including offline replay 61 passed
PostgreSQL recommendation persistence and generation jobs 8 passed against a fresh, dedicated database
Mobile recommendation, refill, explanation, API/cache, and reader tests 84 passed across eight existing test files, after the toolbar expectation fix
Backend load-harness contracts, Linux container with external networking disabled 17 passed
Protected load-workflow validator contracts 65 passed
Full Helm production contract validation Passed
Targeted Dart analysis, Rust formatting, Git whitespace checks Passed

Total: 262 passing automated tests, plus the deployment/static checks above. Logs are retained locally under .local/recommendation-testing-20261122/. An initial database run without TEST_DATABASE_URL skipped coverage and is not counted. The reported database result uses a separate fresh database from the API tests, since worker claims are global and failed fixtures can leave pending jobs.

The database-backed API test exercises opted-in citation generation, exact authorized-page membership, persisted evidence, weighted rollback, stale cursor rejection before enqueueing, shadow without an additional served batch, and local edge retention during a simulated provider failure. Mobile tests cover the three-card refill trigger and stale/canceled results after saves, opt-out, account changes, and revision changes. These are local fixtures, not deployed evidence.

Small compatibility fixes

  • Preserve the existing icon-only comments toolbar. Update its existing test to check the icon while retaining accessible labels, 48-pixel targets, keyboard order, and complete arXiv text.
  • Generate PostgreSQL fixture publication dates at microsecond precision. Windows clocks can have finer precision, causing continuation equality and replay assertions to fail after a database round trip. No runtime ranking or persistence checks were relaxed.
  • Pin the packaged alert-policy JSON to LF in .gitattributes. Windows automatic CRLF conversion changed its bytes and broke the pinned Helm SHA-256 check. The verified LF hash is 1332fab6e5ab0ef0a98a0b74e3d4285ae10764885be9b80e4a6697fb4d42dc46.

No Git merge conflicts were present.

Live OpenAlex: unresolved latency gate

An authenticated HTTPS request to api.openalex.org returned HTTP 200 and three known works in 1,875 ms. The existing production-client live test was attempted twice; both attempts returned Timeout at approximately 1.25 seconds, before reference assertions could run. The client currently allows 1,250 ms per request and 1,500 ms for the complete lookup.

The key was used only in process memory for requests to the official API; captured output was redacted. It is absent from this report and source changes. The production timeout was left unchanged. Local provider-failure fallback tests passed, but this machine has not demonstrated successful live enrichment within the production budget. Recheck the exact deployed candidate from staging before enabling a citation cohort; do not treat the HTTP 200 diagnostic as a passing production-client test.

Remaining protected gates

The production checklist remains unchecked. No Kubernetes context or staging access configuration was found on this machine. The following need the actual protected environment and release artifacts:

  • Reviewed image deployment, schema 26 and replica/configuration convergence; live worker citation edges in both directions, outage/recovery and rollback.
  • Separate authorized queue and proven-empty accounts for measured staging load under both policies, including the stated HTTP percentile and error limits.
  • Measured shadow/cohort invariants, telemetry, completed UTC comparison windows, judgment coverage, save/dismissal outcomes, and a rollout decision.
  • Exact signed Android/iOS candidates, four physical device roles, all 42 scenarios, timing/cache samples, and at least 200 sessions over 24 hours.
  • Remaining protected app-wide production-audit evidence.

Do not mark these gates complete or expand the citation cohort using local test counts or deterministic fixture quality scores as substitutes.

Cleanup

Removed 5,527 build/cache files newly generated during this verification (4,011,025,435 bytes, approximately 4.01 GB), using a file inventory captured before testing. Pre-existing artifacts were preserved. Both dedicated test databases were dropped; the development database and phone installation were unchanged. Test logs and cleanup evidence remain in the local evidence directory.
